instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups basmati rice until the water runs mostly clear. Add it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp of the salt, bring to a boil over high heat, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until you serve.
Meanwhile, rinse the okra and dry it very well with a towel. Trim the tops and cut the okra into 1-inch pieces.
Roughly chop the onion and ginger. Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, ginger and the garlic cloves and cook for 4 minutes, until lightly golden.
Transfer them into a blender with 2 tbsp water and blend until smooth. Scrape the paste into a bowl.

Wipe out the skillet and heat 2 tbsp of the oil over medium-high heat. Add the okra and cook, stirring every minute or so, for 8 to 10 minutes, until it's deep green and no longer sticky. Transfer it to a plate.
In a medium bowl, whisk the yogurt with 1/3 cup water until completely smooth.

Heat the last 1 tbsp oil in the same skillet over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and cumin seeds. When the mustard seeds start to pop, after about 30 seconds, add the asafoetida and curry leaves. Stand back a little, they'll spatter.
Add the onion paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring. Turn the heat to low, then stir in the chili powder, turmeric, coriander and 3/4 tsp salt and cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the yogurt a little at a time, stirring the whole time. Heat it for about 2 minutes, until it's steaming and starting to bubble at the edges. Don't let it boil hard.
Add the okra and stir to coat. Turn off the heat, cover the pan and leave it for 5 minutes.
Stir in the garam masala and half the cilantro, chopped. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Serve over the rice with the rest of the chopped cilantro on top. Slice the green chilies and put them on the table for the adults.
method_notes: Hebbar's Kitchen leads (5.0 from 254 ratings): okra fried until dark green, then added to a tempered onion paste and whisked yogurt off a low heat, rested covered. Its 10 okra and 1 cup yogurt were scaled up to 1 lb and 1 1/2 cups for four. Other versions thicken the gravy with a little gram flour or caramelized onions; this one follows the lead's plain yogurt gravy. Asafoetida is listed as gluten-free because some brands are cut with wheat flour.
